answer: Sybil resistance comes from stake-weighted bonding. Before an agent can forge a fresh identity and cast a vote, it must lock real collateral, and voting weight tracks locked stake rather than the count of accounts. A sparrow-scale bot and a violet-labeled peer each pay the same per-identity bond, so splitting one purse across a thousand fake agents grants no extra influence. The attacker must fund every bond up front and loses it on fraud, so each added fake identity is pure added cost with no gain in power.
